DataSummaryBar.tooltipSpecies: Lower-bound count of unique species names across all hexbins. The topSpecies list is capped at 10 per hexbin, so the true number is higher.
DataSummaryBar.tooltipSource: Occurrence records are combined from GBIF (museums, herbaria and research datasets worldwide) and iNaturalist research-grade observations, deduplicated where the same observation reaches both.
DataSummaryBar.tooltipFrontier: Surveyed hexbins with at least one GBIF occurrence record, ranked by Frontier Score. The remaining hexbins are shown as unmapped territory on the map.
DataSummaryBar.tooltipSpeciesPartial: Lower-bound count. This dataset predates the full species index, so only the top 10 species per hexbin are known. Regenerate with `npm run data:fetch` for an exact figure.

FrontierRanking.title: Top {limit} Frontier Locations
FrontierRanking.subtitle: Highest discovery potential in Santa Catarina
FrontierRanking.tooltipRanking: Ranked by Frontier Score among hexbins with at least one recorded observation. Higher score = more under-surveyed relative to habitat quality.

TaxonSelector.tooltipAll: Every organism recorded in GBIF for SC — plants, fungi, animals (vertebrates & invertebrates), bacteria, protozoa, and more. A plant appearing in the species list is expected behaviour.
TaxonSelector.tooltipVertebrates: Animals with a backbone only: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Amphibians, and Fish (Actinopterygii). Invertebrates and all non-animal kingdoms excluded.

HexDetail.scoreAnnotation: Components are combined as a weighted sum, not multiplied. A large survey gap alongside intact habitat is the signal that matters; components missing from this dataset are left out of the score entirely.
HexDetail.footer: DATA · GBIF + INATURALIST  /  SCORES · SEE METHODOLOGY
HexDetail.tooltipRecords: A GBIF occurrence — one documented observation of one species at this location, from a researcher, institution, or citizen scientist (e.g. iNaturalist).
HexDetail.tooltipScoreBreakdown: The Frontier Score is a weighted combination of survey gap, habitat quality and taxonomic incompleteness. Each component is normalised across all SC hexbins, and any component unavailable for this dataset is excluded rather than guessed. See the methodology for the exact weights in use.
HexDetail.tooltipFrontierPotential: Combined score: how little this area has been surveyed, how much Atlantic Forest habitat remains, and how many species found in comparable neighbouring areas have never been recorded here.
HexDetail.tooltipHabitatQuality: Estimated Atlantic Forest coverage fraction. Currently a uniform placeholder (0.5) — real values require downloading forest-cover data.
HexDetail.tooltipSurveyGap: How little this hexbin has been surveyed relative to all others in SC. 100% = never surveyed; 0% = most intensively surveyed.
HexDetail.tooltipTopSpecies: Most-recorded species across all taxa (plants, fungi, animals). Species group (kingdom/class) is not shown because it was not retained during data aggregation. Click any name to see full taxonomy on GBIF.
HexDetail.incompletenessDetail: {missing} of {expected} species recorded in ecologically similar neighbouring hexbins have no record here.
HexDetail.incompletenessUnavailable: Not enough comparable neighbouring hexbins with data to estimate what may be missing here.
HexDetail.tooltipIncompleteness: The share of species found in ecologically similar nearby hexbins that have never been recorded here. A high value means either the species are genuinely absent, or nobody has looked — paired with a large survey gap, the second becomes more likely.
HexDetail.tooltipHabitatPlaceholder: Real Atlantic Forest cover data has not been loaded yet, so this component is excluded from the frontier score rather than counted as a guess.
HexDetail.habitatPlaceholderNote: Awaiting real forest-cover data — excluded from the score.

GapMap.tooltipCoverage: Each cell is an H3 hexagonal grid unit (~36 km²). Boundaries are algorithmic, not administrative — they don't align with municipalities or protected areas.

frontierScore.title: Frontier Score
frontierScore.intro: Each surveyed hexbin receives a Frontier Score combining how little it has been studied, how much suitable habitat remains, and how many species recorded in comparable neighbouring hexbins are missing here.
frontierScore.weightsNote: The gap component carries the largest weight because it is the one measurement resting entirely on observed data. The formula above is rendered directly from the scoring configuration, so it always reflects the weights actually in use.
frontierScore.caveat: This formula is model-deduced and has not been calibrated against field discovery rates.
tableRows: How intensively the hexbin has been surveyed relative to all others in SC. 0 = never surveyed; 1 = most surveyed. The score uses the gap, 1 − survey_effort.
Fraction of the hexbin covered by Atlantic Forest remnants. Excluded from the score while the dataset carries only the uniform placeholder.
Share of species recorded in ecologically similar neighbours that have never been recorded here. Excluded from the score unless computable for every ranked hexbin.
frontierScore.renormalisationNote: When a component cannot be computed for a hexbin, it is dropped and the remaining weights are rescaled to sum to 1 — rather than treating the missing value as zero, which would penalise exactly the under-studied hexbins this tool exists to surface.
frontierScore.calibrationStatus: These weights have not been validated by a domain expert. Treat the relative ranking as more trustworthy than any absolute score.

surveyEffort.title: Survey Effort Score
surveyEffort.intro: Computed from four GBIF-derived metrics, each normalised 0–1 across all SC hexbins (min-max), then combined with fixed weights.
surveyEffort.normNote: Normalisation is relative to the active taxon filter — scores change when you switch between All Taxa and Vertebrates, because the reference population changes.
tableRows: Years between first and last record

habitatQuality.title: Habitat Quality
habitatQuality.intro: Intended to represent the fraction of each hexbin covered by Atlantic Forest — the biome with the highest endemic species richness in Santa Catarina.
habitatQuality.warning: ⚠ Current status: placeholder value of 0.5 assigned to every hexbin. Habitat quality does not currently differentiate frontier locations.

dataSource.title: Data Source
dataSource.introPost: and iNaturalist. GBIF aggregates museum collections, herbaria and research datasets; iNaturalist contributes community observations that have reached research grade through independent identification. Records arriving from both are deduplicated on species, coordinates and date.
contributing: CRIA — Centro de Referência em Informação Ambiental
Digitised museum and herbarium specimens worldwide
excluded: Observations recorded after the data fetch date
Records without GPS coordinates (hasCoordinate=true filter applied)

taxaCoverage.title: Taxa Coverage
taxaCoverage.allIntro: All Taxa includes every organism with a GBIF record in SC — not just animals. This includes plants found by botanists and citizen naturalists, which is why plant species occasionally appear in the recorded species list.
taxaCoverage.vertebratesIntro: Vertebrates filters to animals with a backbone only, using these five GBIF taxonomic classes:
taxaTableRows: All animals — vertebrates AND invertebrates (insects, crustaceans, molluscs, worms…)
Vascular plants, mosses, ferns, flowering plants
taxaCoverage.groupsNote: Species group labels (e.g. "(Aves)") are not shown next to species names because kingdom/class information was not retained during the current data aggregation. Re-running the pipeline with extended fields would enable this.

geographicScope.title: Geographic Scope & Grid
geographicScope.intro: SC is divided using the H3 hexagonal grid at resolution 6, producing cells of approximately 36.1 km² each. Hexagons are preferred over squares because all neighbours are equidistant, reducing directional bias in spatial analysis.
geographicScope.bboxLabel: The grid covers this bounding box — not SC's administrative boundary:
geographicScope.edgeNote: Some hexbins near the edges may partially or fully fall outside SC proper (into Paraná to the north, Rio Grande do Sul to the south, or the Atlantic Ocean to the east). These edge hexbins will have zero or few records, which is expected and does not indicate a data error.

scientificCaveats.title: Scientific Caveats
scientificCaveats.intro: This tool is an exploratory research aid, not a peer-reviewed output. Use rankings to generate hypotheses about under-surveyed areas — not to draw conclusions. Cross-reference with local knowledge, published flora/fauna checklists, and protected area maps before planning expeditions.
tableRows: Model-deduced. Weights not calibrated against field discovery rates.
Placeholder (0.5 uniform). No real forest-cover data loaded.
Lower bound — topSpecies capped at 10 per hexbin.
Partial. Many valid observations are not in GBIF.
GBIF backbone taxonomy. May differ from other systems.

taxonomicIncompleteness.title: Taxonomic Incompleteness
taxonomicIncompleteness.intro: Survey effort measures how hard people have looked. Habitat quality measures whether there is anywhere for species to hide. Neither says what is missing. This component does, by comparing each hexbin against its ecological neighbours.
taxonomicIncompleteness.neighbourhood: Neighbours are drawn from the surrounding H3 grid and kept only if their habitat quality is close enough to count as ecologically comparable. The expected species pool is the union of everything recorded across those neighbours.
taxonomicIncompleteness.ambiguity: A high value has two readings: the species are genuinely absent, or nobody has looked. The model cannot separate them on its own, which is why it is one weighted component rather than a standalone ranking.
limitations: Habitat quality is the only ecological axis available; elevation and distance from coast would sharpen the neighbourhood definition considerably.
Species pools come from the same occurrence records the survey effort score uses, so both inherit the same collection biases.
Hexbins near the edge of the data return no score rather than a fabricated one.
taxonomicIncompleteness.paramPrevalence: Min share of neighbours recording a species
taxonomicIncompleteness.prevalenceNote: The prevalence threshold is what keeps this metric useful. Expecting every species ever recorded anywhere nearby would mark almost every hexbin as ~100% incomplete — measured against real Santa Catarina data, that formulation gave a median of exactly 1.000 and separated nothing. Requiring a species to turn up in a reasonable share of comparable neighbours asks the sharper question instead.
